en: The Apadāna of the Elder Sīhāsanadāyaka Kumuda Chapter 5.5 The Apadāna of the Elder Sīhāsanadāyaka: In the past, during the time of the Buddha Kassapa, I was a king named Jayasena, ruling over the earth. There, in the city of Bandhumatī, I built a magnificent hall, And within it, I fashioned a lion-throne made of gold. When the Teacher, the Great Sage, arrived there, I offered that lion-throne to the Buddha. Because of that gift of a lion-throne, For ninety-one eons I never fell from heaven. Having passed through those many hundreds of thousands of eons, I have now attained this final existence. Through the merit of offering that lion-throne, I have been reborn in a noble family. Now, having become a monk under the dispensation of Gotama, I have realized the state of an Arhat. By the power of that same meritorious deed, I am now free from all suffering. Thus did the Elder Sīhāsanadāyaka speak of his own past deeds.
“When the Protector of the World, the Leader Padumuttara, had attained Nibbāna,
with a clear heart and a joyful mind,
which brings happiness pertaining to the present life, along with many perfumes and garlands.
many people attain Nibbāna with a serene heart and a joyful mind.
Having paid homage to the supreme Bodhi,
for a hundred thousand aeons I did not fall into an unhappy destination.
In the fifteenth thousand aeons, eight of them were named Siluccaya.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Sīhāsanadāyaka recited these verses.
This is the fifth legend of the elder Sīhāsanadāyaka.
